page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine based on the Dlsv6 series, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores via hyperthreading. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocking up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates a massive 260 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is fixed at 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage disks, requiring remote Premium Storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong processing efficiency across both single-threaded and parallel workloads. The system achieves high tier results in Geekbench 6 with a single-core score of 2042.0 and a multi-core score of 16898.0, reinforced by upper-quartile ratings in physics simulations and image processing. Large-block uncached read bandwidth registers at 205.24 GB/sec, reflecting efficient memory subsystem utilization. Furthermore, integrated AMX matrix acceleration supports notable small-model language generation, achieving 347.06 tokens per second in 135M text generation benchmarks.

Because the D32ls_v6 allocates a reduced memory footprint compared to standard 1:4 memory configurations, it offers enhanced resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks that do not require extensive RAM. The lack of ephemeral local storage shifts all IO overhead to remote managed disks, which administrators must provision according to performance needs. The instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, CPU-based lightweight AI inference, web serving, and parallel integer computational workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is a virtual machine profile powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache and 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a compute-dense 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It incorporates vector and tensor acceleration via AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The server contains no onboard GPUs and provides no local scratch storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage. Benchmark performance indicates upper-quartile execution in Geekbench compute tasks, uncached memory read bandwidth, and static web serving throughput reaching 55.94 GB/sec. Given its lean memory configuration, the instance offers cost-efficient compute capacity for parallel processing, software build farms, web serving layers, and small-model CPU inference pipelines.
